A change to `NEW_INFO` or `NON_BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO` also raises an alert and sends `dbs-rtw.alert.raised`. submission_id.description: The questionnaire the document belongs to; null for a candidate's standing document.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref` (Hub uuid), the same value the APIs use.

document_id.description: The id of the document: the `ftw` path parameter of the download.

source.description: Where the document belongs: `submission` (the request's own) or `candidate` (the candidate's standing document). Pass it as `source` when downloading.

kind.description: `ftw_certificate` for a Fit to Work certificate or `fail_letter` for a fail letter.

dataSchema.description:
A request is waiting for the candidate. It is sent in two situations, and `awaiting` tells them apart. When a request is created with an online questionnaire that Hub has a form for, it is sent straight after `request.submitted`, with `awaiting` set to `questionnaire` and `form` naming the first questionnaire the candidate has to complete; the request is emailed to Healthier Business only once that questionnaire is in. When a reviewer asks the candidate for more information (a request needs a document or an answer), it is sent again with the questionnaire's `submission_reference`, `form` and `has_review_note`, and `awaiting` is absent.

The reviewer's note is health data and is never in the body: `has_review_note` only says whether one exists. Read it with `GET /requests/{id}`. For the first situation you can answer the questionnaire for the candidate with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` (see `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`), or leave it to the candidate, who has been emailed. The request leaves this state with `request.questionnaire_completed` or an outcome event.

The data carries the `candidate_ref`, the course ids and names and `assigned_at`; it never carries the candidate's name or email. Credits are not part of the event: for the credits an assignment took, read the answer of the API call or `GET /credits/transactions`. A failure to queue the event never undoes the assignment.

When it fires: when a learner passes a course (the result is recorded), or when staff mark the course complete in Hub. One event per course passed, so a candidate finishing three courses causes three events; the event for the last of their assigned courses is followed by `online-training.training.completed`. Who gets it: every active endpoint of the client that picked `online-training.course.completed`.

The data holds the `candidate_ref`, the course id and name, the dates and the `grade` from 0 to 1 (rounded to four decimals), and `expires_at`, the date the certificate runs out and the course is due for renewal. A renewal completed later sends a new event for the same course. No name or email is included: fetch `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}/results/{course_id}` for more.

expires_at.description: When the certificate expires and the course is due for renewal.
